thread:
anya: Heads up — we started getting alerts ~09:02 UTC: p95 gen latency for dedicated-eu jumped from ~120ms to ~650ms and throughput dropped ~40% on pool eu-dedicated-2 :alarm:
mike: I see the spikes in the console too. Any rollout around that time? /cc @kevin
kevin: No deploys from infra around 09:00. I pulled recent commits — only a small batching heuristic tweak landed from eng/runtime at 08:53. Could be related.
sam: Which heuristic? the new pack-by-length change? That one coalesces short + long requests into single batch.
anya: Yeah that one. I'm seeing a pattern: lots of requests routed to slot type A (8GB) instead of B (16GB) after packing. Slots A can't hold KV for the long sequences so cache eviction rate skyrockets.
mike: Logs show frequent KV cache evict/alloc churn. Snippet from node logs:
```
[09:04:12] kv_cache: evict shard=5 entries=1200 reason=oom
[09:04:12] kernel: fallback=matmul_slow path=quantized->float
[09:04:12] scheduler: batch_size=48 latency_ms=642
```
kevin: Oof. Kernel fallback and cache thrash together = perf death spiral. Why were requests routed to A? packing heuristic should respect slot affinity.
sam: There's a placement rule in the dedicated routing service that caps `max_batch_bytes` per slot; but I found a config mismatch: dedicated quota agent was using `max_batch_bytes=0` (meaning no cap) for pool eu-dedicated-2 after yesterday's quota change. That allowed aggressive packing into small slots.
anya: So two problems: heuristic packs heterogeneous sequences together, then quota misconfig removes protection so scheduler stuffs them into smaller slots, which then thrash KV, kernel falls back, latency spikes.
mike: Confirmed with profiler: CPU/GPU timeline shows tons of small matmuls and poor kernel choice at 09:03-09:07. I exported the trace and ran `nvprof` style summary — 85% of time in fallback kernels.
kevin: Quick mitigation idea: revert pack-by-length heuristic, enforce per-slot batch byte cap, and throttle new long requests to higher-slot types. Can we patch live?
sam: I submitted a hotfix to routing to set `max_batch_bytes=16000` for eu-dedicated-2 and rolled the change at 09:18. Also temporarily disabled the packing rule at 09:21.
eng-bot: deploy: routing-config-change applied to pool eu-dedicated-2 by sam at 09:18 UTC — success
anya: After the fix p95 dropped to ~130ms and throughput recovered ~95% by 09:30. KV evictions returned to baseline.
mike: Can you paste the profiling outputs? we need an RCA doc.
kevin: Summary from the perf dump:
- root cause: packing heuristic allowed heterogeneous sequence coalescing without affinity check
- contributing: quota config change removed max_batch_bytes protection for pool
- effect: small-slot placement -> KV eviction thrash -> kernel fallback to slower matmuls -> sustained latency/throughput regression
- detection: alerts triggered by p95 and slot eviction rate metrics
- impact: ~38% throughput drop for 28 minutes, SLA windows crossed for 2 customers on pool
sam: PRs: 1) revert heuristic (eng/runtime#412), 2) add placement guard in routing to respect slot KV capacity (eng-platform#879), 3) add config validation so max_batch_bytes cannot be 0 for dedicated pools (infra#1203).
anya: Also adding monitoring: eviction_rate_alert, kernel-fallback-rate, and a canary that simulates mixed-length traffic.
mike: Action items assigned:
- kevin: lead RCA writeup and postmortem (due EOD)
- sam: follow up PRs and config validation (in progress)
- anya: add canary job and dashboards for eviction and kernel fallback (ETA tomorrow)
- eng-sre (oncall-sre): reach out to affected customers with incident summary and mitigation
oncall-sre: I'll open the incident ticket and draft the customer note. Noting SLA breach for two customers — need approver for outreach.
kevin: Adding retrospective: we should test packing heuristics against mixed-slot topologies in CI, and add a pre-apply config lint that rejects `max_batch_bytes=0` for dedicated pools.
sam: One more note — scheduler logs showed some placement retries due to transient quota KB errors; I'll add exponential backoff and rejection path so we don't overpack when quota state ambiguous.
mike: Thanks. Marking this thread resolved for now but leave open until postmortem posted. :white_check_mark:
